Guaranteed Amount 
The Guaranteed Amount can be entered on the Interest Conditions (INTSM) screen. With credit 
interest this will be the minimum interest payable to the client. For debit interest it will be the 
maximum interest chargeable to the client. 
Level Usage 
If the account is using the 'Simple' method of calculating interest, the way in which interest can be 
charged or paid on an account is controlled by the entry you make in the “Level Usage” field. The 
interest rate can be based on its balance. Up to four interest levels can be defined for this purpose. 
Each level has a maximum amount up to which an interest rate or rate variation is applied.  
Interest levels can be applied in three ways: 
• 
On an All-Up basis, the interest rate for the level in which the balance falls is applied to the 
whole balance 
• 
On a Slice basis, the interest rate for each level is applied to the part of the balance that falls 
in that level 
• 
On a Flat rate basis, where Interest Rate 1 is used as the flat rate. 
 
If the account is using the 'Compound' method of calculating interest, then interest levels are not 
applicable, and a Flat rate must be used. 
Each interest bearing account can have a minimum and maximum interest rate associated with it. 
If the interest rate on an account is linked to a base rate and the gross interest rate falls below the 
minimum, the minimum rate is used. If it exceeds the maximum, the maximum rate is used.

Closing a Client Account 
A single screen is provided to handle account closure. This is the Close Client Account (CACLS) 
screen. It gives details of the current status of the account with regard to balance, charges and 
interest outstanding and enables you specify a destination account for the final balance. 
When an account has been closed using the Close Client Account (CACLS) screen, the account is 
purged after the period you have specified using the retention period parameter CASTM (see 
“Retention Parameters” in the Guide to Setting Up). Note that when an account has been closed 
the account details cannot be changed. 
Close Client Account (CACLS) 
This screen is used to close an active client account. If any forward valued postings exist for the 
account you are prevented from closing it until all postings have come to value. Furthermore, if it 
has an outstanding balance, interest to be debited or credited or if account charges are to be levied, 
another (transfer) account must be identified to which these can be posted prior to closure. 
If the account being closed has been used for standing orders, then another method must be 
established to enable these to continue. For example, you can set up an alternative account to deal 
with them. 
Before closing an account, the ‘Charge Calculation’ and ‘Guaranteed Amount’ values - set up on 
the Interest Conditions (INTSM) screen - must be set at ‘2’ and ‘0’ respectively. This ensures that 
the correct interest is settled during end-of-day processing. 
Interest settlement accounts can be closed, but note that any postings to such an account when 
closed will be redirected to the error suspense account. 
When you have entered details of the account being closed you will be asked to confirm that you 
are closing the account you intended to close. Once you have closed the account you cannot make 
amendments to it.

Outstanding Balances and Interest 
The balance outstanding is displayed automatically and posted, on-line, to the transfer account. 
The interest outstanding is displayed automatically. Outstanding interest is settled overnight

If interest is outstanding, the following message is displayed:

settlement frequency originally set up for the account. 
If the account being closed is also the account to which interest settlement was normally made, 
then the interest settlement (on closure) must be sent to the transfer account. This is done 
automatically by changing the settlement method on the Client Account Maintenance (CAHDR) 
screen and settlement account entries on the Client Account Static Details (WACCM) screen. If 
interest is normally settled in another valid client account or error suspense account, settlement (on

Transfer Account Field 
If outstanding balances, debit/credit interest or any charges exist then a separate transfer account, 
to which these are to be posted, must be identified before an account can be closed. Otherwise this 
is not a mandatory field. 
The transfer account is validated as follows: 
• 
It must be a real client or general ledger account 
• 
It must not be a backing or control general ledger account 
• 
It must not be blocked for both credits and debits 
• 
It must not be blocked for credits if a credit transfer is being made 
• 
It must not be blocked for debits if a debit transfer is being made 
 
Charges Outstanding Field 
Charges outstanding are displayed automatically. Account charges are settled into the settlement 
account determined by the charge settlement method on the Client Account Maintenance 
(CAHDR) screen. 
Effect of Closure 
After a client account has been closed, automatic postings in respect of the account (generated by 
contracts, for example) are made to the error suspense account.  If the account being closed is an 
interest settlement account, any postings for the account are made to the error suspense account. 
On closure of an account, the system automatically updates the following values on the Client 
Account Maintenance (CAHDR) and Client Account Static Details (WACCM) screens: 
• 
The credit and debit interest settlement frequencies are set to daily 
• 
The statement frequency is set to daily 
• 
The interest statement required is set to ‘automatic’ if it was previously 'request' 
 
On closure of an account, the following reports should be run under their default options: 
• 
CASTMTS - Client Account Statements, which produces on-request statements for specific 
client accounts. A statement is produced for each account whose frequency is “due” or 
“overdue”. The account status, for closed accounts, is displayed accordingly. 
• 
CAINT - Client Account Interest Statements, which produces on-request interest statements 
for accounts, identifies those accounts that are closed. 
 
If further copies of statements are required for closed accounts, the appropriate Run Time options 
must be used.

Entering Batched Postings 
The following screens are used to enter batched postings: 
• 
Batch Header (BHEAD) screen, used to open a batch 
• 
Client Account Credit (CACR) and Client Account Debit screens (CADR), used to enter 
credits and debits to client accounts 
• 
Client Account Credit Control (CACCN) and Client Account Debit Control (CADCN), used 
to control credits and debits to client accounts 
• 
Client Account Debit Cheque (CADCQ), used to enter cheque details 
• 
Management Services Transaction Maintenance (CATRM) to enter a paired transaction and 
Management Services Transaction Narratives (PNARM) to enter the narratives related to a 
paired transaction 
• 
Batch Close (BCLOS) screen, used to close a batch 
 
If blueprint parameter BP-OVDR-CONT has been set to 'Y' (see "Blueprint Parameters" in the 
Guide to Setting Up), the client account's overdraft limit is applied to batches of postings entered 
via the batch posting screens. If a debit posting in the batch will cause the overdraft limit to be 
exceeded, then it will not be possible to close the batch until the overdraft limit is increased using 
the Client Account Static Details (WACCM) screen.

Batch Close (BCLOS) for Client Accounting 
This screen is used to close a batch of postings to client accounts. The following expected values 
must be entered if you wish to reconcile the batch: 
• 
Number of credit items 
• 
Credit total 
• 
Number of debit items 
• 
Debit total 
 
If these values are different to those calculated by the system, the calculated values are displayed. 
If the batch consists of mixed currency postings, add the amounts of the postings together, 
regardless of the actual currency of each, to make the credit and debit totals. For example, if you 
enter the following postings: 
• 
Credit 100,000 GBP 
• 
Credit 400,000 USD 
• 
Debit 50,000 GBP 
• 
Debit 100,000 USD 
 
This gives a debit total of 150,000 and a credit total of 500,000. The system then checks that the 
totals you have entered agree with the totals it has calculated. 
If a client account was entered, the batch can only be closed as “reconciled” if the expected and 
calculated values are the same. If a general ledger contra account was entered on the Batch Header 
(BHEAD) screen, the system permits the total credit and debit amounts to differ.

for reopening an unreconciled closed batch is described in the explanation of the “Batch Header 
(BHEAD) for Client Accounts” earlier in this section. 
If you wish to reconcile a batch, you must enter the total credit and debit amounts and the total 
credit and debit items. 
When a batch contains either back-valued paired transactions or those that require a negative 
balance check, then these transactions will be removed from the batch when it is closed. They will 
then be moved to an authorisation queue. You can view this queue from the Management Services 
Queue (BANQI) screen. Paired transactions belong to the Client Account Management Services

Setting Up and Maintaining Account Charges 
The procedure for setting up and maintaining account charges is described below, using the 
following screens: 
• 
The General Purpose Narratives (GNARR) screen is used to set up charge types and charge 
conditions, using table types CT and CH respectively 
• 
The Charge Codes Maintenance (CACCM) screen is used to set up and maintain charge 
codes. For each charge condition, a number of charge codes relating to different posting types 
are defined. Each charge code within a charge condition has an associated amount and 
effective date 
• 
The Account Charges Static Details (CACHM) screen is used to enter details of account 
charges, and conditions. These may be linked to a specific client account or to an accounting 
centre. Charge conditions are used to define: 
− Frequency of charges 
− Minimum amount to be charged for a charge period 
− Offset interest details. This is a way of reducing charges for clients whose accounts remain 
in credit. A notional interest amount is calculated, based on the credit balance; this is 
deducted from the calculated charge amount and only the net difference is charged to the 
client 
− Minimum balances. Accounts that remain at or above defined minimum balances will  
not incur charges 
• 
The Client Account Static Details (WACCM) screen is used to allocate the charge conditions 
so that they become effective on the appropriate client account; also to identify the accounts 
to which charges are settled 
• 
Account Charges Screen Defaults (CACSM) is used to set up and maintain screen defaults for 
account charges 
• 
Account Charges Review and Post (CACRP) is used to review charge amounts for specific 
client accounts. Charges are calculated during overnight processing. The charges are then 
available to be reviewed and, if necessary, they can be changed manually before they are 
posted 
− charges may be reviewed, for each client account, before they are posted 
− alternatively, all charges due up to a specified date may be accepted 
 
The above screens are described on the following pages, with the exception of: 
• 
The General Purpose Narratives table (GNARR); see the Guide to Setting Up 
• 
The Client Account Static Details (WACCM) screen; see “Setting up and Maintaining Client 
Accounts”

Funds held until an expiry date is released as part of the Start of Day processing on the expiry 
date. See the Overnight Reports Guide for more information on the overnight report run.

Section 5     
Automatic Payments    
Introduction  
Standing orders may be drawn against any type of account (including general ledger accounts). 
The beneficiary of the funds from a standing order can be a client of: 
• 
Your own institution (internal) 
• 
An external bank that is a member of the supported clearing system (domestic) 
• 
An external bank that is not a member of the supported clearing system (foreign) 
  
When a standing order is debited in favour of an external beneficiary, the client’s account is 
debited and an entry placed in a file of clearing credits during overnight processing. There are 
separate files for domestic and foreign accounts. 
You can set up the following types of standing order: 
• 
Client Account to Client Account 
• 
Client Account to external third party account 
• 
Client Account to General Ledger 
• 
General Ledger to General Ledger 
• 
General Ledger to Client Account 
• 
General Ledger to external third party account 
 
For standing orders that apply to general ledger accounts, you can apply the transfer to an account 
set up for all accounting centres and/or all currencies (where the payment type, described below, is 
“Full Balance”). This enables transfers on either a “many to one” or a “many to many” basis, and 
so avoids the need for repetitive data-entry. 
For all the new standing orders, you can set a 12 digit Standing Order number by setting a value 
for the blueprint BP-SO-PFX. The format is ppffffff0000, where the value (2 digit) set for the 
blueprint is used as the prefix followed by 4 digit Standing Order number with 6 digit number 
incrementing from 000001 for every clean payment created. If the set value is 0 (default) then the 
system will continue to generate 10 digit standing order number.

Processing Standing Orders 
Once a standing order has been successfully created in the system, it undergoes balance checking 
before being posted to the account. If the standing order is to an external account, then S.W.I.F.T. 
messages are created.  
Balance checking is performed to ensure sufficient funds are available in the debit account. If 
there are sufficient funds, processing proceeds as normal. If funds are not available, the standing 
order is sent to the authorisation queue. Standing orders that are debiting General Ledger accounts 
do not undergo balance checking.  
The authorisation queue for standing orders can be viewed using the Standing Order Authorisation 
Queue (SOAHI) screen. You can then choose the standing orders to authorise on the Standing 
Orders Input (SOSTM) screen. 
The authorisation queue for clean payments can be viewed using the Clean Payments from 
Standing Orders (SOPRQ) screen. To view internal or external standing order products on the 
queue, enter a product based on the following contract types: 
• 
SOEX for external standing orders  
• 
SOSO for internal standing orders  
 
You can choose the standing orders to authorise on the Clean Payments Authorisation (CPAUT) 
screen. See the Settlements Guide for more information on this screen. 
For accounts that require a Negative Balance Check before postings are debited from that account, 
there is a different process for balance checking, described in Standing Orders and Client Account 
Management Services below. 
Once the standing order has been authorised, the CPAYMENTS - Clean Payment Processing 
report deals with processing of the payments. For payments to external accounts, this report also 
creates S.W.I.F.T. messages, which must be authorised before release on the Authorise Release of 
Event Messages (SETTA) screen, described in the Settlements Guide.  
Standing Orders and Client Account Management Services 
Client Account Management Services (CMS) are a set of optional functions in the system that 
allows greater control of client accounts. One of these functions is Negative Balance Checking, 
and any standing order due to be debited to an account marked as requiring a negative balance 
check is affected. For full details of CMS, see Appendix C of this guide.  
After a debit payment to an account that requires a negative balance check has been authorised, it 
is moved onto a Pending Queue, acquiring the status of 'Pending'. Once on the queue, the payment 
can be released in the following ways: 
• 
The system can release a payment when sufficient funds are available on the account. The 
sleeping report RELPENDQ - Release from Pending Queue handles this automatically (this 
report is described in the On-Demand Reports Guide).  
• 
You can force the release of a payment, regardless of sufficient funds being available. This is 
done from the Management Services Queue (BANQI) screen, described in Appendix C of this

Once the payment has been released from the pending queue, it is processed in the same way as

When creating an MT103 or MT202, you should complete the details on the Standing Orders

Notes: The Cross Currency “Exchange Rate”, “Bought Accounting Centre” and “Sold

The “Transfer/Minimum Amount” and “Transfer Type” fields are only mandatory when the

When the Debit Account is a client account, the account's general ledger backing account is used

To enter the extended narrative, double mouse click the Notepad icon next to narrative field and

Payment Type Field 
Each payment amount must be identified as being of a certain type (“Payment Type”), using one 
of five options. The amount entered as the “Payment Amount” is transferred according to this 
payment type, as follows: 
• 
Fixed Amount (AM) 
A stated fixed amount (“Payment Amount”) is to be transferred 
• 
Full Balance (FL) 
The whole balance of the account is to be transferred, leave “Payment Amount” blank 
• 
Minimum Balance (MN) 
The amount required to “top up” an account to a stated minimum balance is to be transferred.  
Enter the minimum balance in the “Payment Amount” field 
• 
Maximum Amount (MX) 
The balance in full, up to a stated maximum amount, is to be transferred. Enter the maximum 
value in the “Payment Amount” field 
• 
Above Maximum Balance (OA) 
The amount above a stated maximum balance is to be transferred. Enter the value of the 
maximum balance in the “Payment Amount” field 
 
The numbers 1, 2 and 3 are used to relate payment types with the different payments involved with 
the standing order, as follows: 
• 
1 - First Payment 
• 
2 - Interim Payments 
• 
3 - Final Payment 
 
You must enter the first payment amount; if you do not enter amounts 2 and 3 the system assumes 
you wish to make equal payments and uses the first payment amount for the interim and final 
payments. 
Both the payment amount and type can be amended at any time prior to the first payment. Once a 
payment has been made the amount cannot be changed.

Payment and Transfer Type 
With Payment Type “Above Maximum Balance”, Standing Orders can be limited to those that 
involve significant amounts only. This reduces the extent to which transfers of amounts that are 
not fixed are made when the amounts themselves are so small as to limit the usefulness of the 
standing order. The amount of the balance you wish to maintain is entered under “Payment 
Amount”. Any amount above this value is transferred only if it is not less than the 
“Transfer/Minimum Amount”. 
With Payment Type “Minimum Balance” standing orders may be similarly limited to significant 
amounts, or you can define conditions that ensure that accounts are only “topped up” when 
necessary and by minimum transfer amounts. The amount of the balance you wish to maintain is 
entered under “Payment Amount”. If the account balance is below this value a transfer is made to 
the account, in order to make up the balance, subject to the following conditions associated with 
Transfer Type codes: 
Exceeds 
The posting takes place only if the amount to be transferred to make up the balance 
is greater than that entered under “Transfer/Minimum Amount”. 
Less Than 
The amount to be transferred is equal to the value entered as the 
“Transfer/Minimum Amount”, irrespective of the actual amount required to make 
up the balance. 
Plus 
The amount to be transferred is equal to the actual amount required to make up the 
balance, plus the value entered under “Transfer/Minimum Amount”. 
 
For the Payment Types "Fixed Amount", "Full Balance" and "Maximum Amount" you should not 
enter a Transfer Type and Transfer/Minimum Amount.

Holiday Method 
This comprises two fields. The first identifies the method that 
the system uses to determine the settlement event date, if 
the system generated event date falls on a holiday in the 
countries indicated by the value in the second field.  
The first field indicates one of the following: 
Following (F) 
The system settles the amount on the next available day. 
Modified (M) 
The system settles the amount on the next available day. If this 
falls in the following month, the system will search for the first 
available day prior to the end of the month. 
Previous (P) 
The system settles the amount on the first available previous 
day. 
None (N) 
The system will settle on the event day, even if it is a holiday. 
The second field contains a value defined on the Country Check 
Codes table (CNCHK) representing the currencies to be 
checked for holidays for each contract event.

Interest Basis 
Interest Calculation 
Basis 
 
This is the method of calculating interest over a year. 
360 - 1/360th of the annual interest is charged per elapsed day 
365 - 1/365th of the annual interest is charged per elapsed day 
366 - For leap years only, 1/366th of the annual interest is 
charged per elapsed day 
12 - Annual interest is divided by 12 and applied on a whole

Definition 
Level Usage 
 
The way in which interest can be charged or paid on an account 
is controlled by the entry you make in this field. The interest rate 
can be based on its balance. Up to four interest levels can be 
defined for this purpose. Each level has a maximum amount up 
to which an interest rate or rate variation is applied. 
Interest levels can be applied in two ways: 
• 
On an All-Up basis, the interest rate for the level in which 
the balance falls is applied to the whole balance 
• 
On a Slice basis, the interest rate for each level is applied to 
the part of the balance that falls in that level 
 
A Flat rate of interest can also be applied.  
If you are calculating interest using the ‘'Compound’' method, 
then interest levels are not applicable, and a flat rate must be 
applied.  
Each interest bearing account can have a minimum and 
maximum interest rate associated with it. If the interest rate on 
an account falls below the minimum, the minimum rate is used. 
If it exceeds the maximum, the maximum rate is used. 
• 
All-Up (A) 
• 
Slice (S) 
• 
Flat (F) 
 
The interest level is set for an account product and cannot be 
changed for a specific account.

Availability of Deposited Funds 
The system provides the capability of controlling the availability of deposited funds in accordance

Narrative (GNARR) tables, type ST and FA.

input into the Narrative field on the Client Account Credit (CACR) screen (see Section 4), when 
you are entering details of the deposit.

banking regulations and the holds can be viewed using the Hold Funds Inquiry (HOLDI) screen.

Narrative Key contains the deposit code, the Narrative Text contains an algorithm for the clearing 
days. The first three characters of the Narrative Text represent the number of business days to 
clear the funds for an existing client; the second three characters represent the number of business 
days to clear the funds for a new client. 
Note: - If a deposit code occurs in table ST but not in table FA, then United States banking 
regulations are not applied.

Appendix C   
Client Account Management Services  
Introduction 
Client Account Management Services (CMS) is a set of functions that allows a designated user 
more control over marked accounts. The following functionality is available: 
• 
Production of Account Analysis reports, which perform the following functions: 
- Displaying information on an account 
- Tracking of the transactions posted to an account 
- Grouping together of charges into a monthly total charge amount 
• 
Maintenance of account target balances in a hierarchy of accounts  
• 
Checking of account balances before transactions are posted to marked accounts to ensure 
sufficient funds are available. This is known as negative balance checking 
• 
Immediate posting of charges made to a client account during transactions 
 
The tracking of transactions, negative balance checking and immediate posting of charges features 
require batched postings to client accounts to be made using only Paired Transactions. A paired 
transaction consists of the original posting, and a balancing posting to a contra account (which can 
be either a client or general ledger account). Paired Transactions are described later in this section.  
The CMS functionality cannot be used in conjunction with the Batch Authorisation functionality 
described in Section 4 of this guide.

Charges in Account Analysis 
When an account is marked as requiring Account Analysis, the charges that are made of the 
account can be posted in the following ways: 
• 
Charges can be collected into a Monthly Payment Charge, which can then be reviewed, and 
posted.  
• 
Charges can be reviewed, adjusted if necessary, and posted individually to the account. 
All charges must be defined on the Account Charges Static Details (CACHM) screen, then linked 
to an account and transaction type on the Management Services Transactions for Analysis 
(TRCKM) screen. 
When they have been generated via the CAACANAL - Account Analysis Statement report, all 
charges must be viewed and released via the Account Charges Review and Post (CACRP) screen. 
By entering a Client Account number on this screen, an individual charge can be reviewed and the 
amount adjusted if required. If the amount is set to zero, then the charge will be waived and not 
posted. After an individual charge has been reviewed the status will change to ‘R’ (Reviewed).  
Once all individual charges that require review have been processed, all remaining charges can be 
automatically marked as reviewed by entering a Charge Settlement Date of Today. This will 
change the status of all remaining charges to ‘R’ (Reviewed).   
The Charges Posting (CACHPOST) report must be initiated in sleeping mode and will process all 
charges with a status of ‘R’. 
Any charges that will settle to client accounts with a Negative Balance Checking (NBC) indicator 
(see Negative Balance Checking) will have their status changed to ‘W’ (Pending) instead of ‘R’ 
and a record will be created on the Pending Queue. These charges will be released in accordance 
with the NBC rules, either automatically by the RELPENDQ sleeping report or manually ‘Rushed’ 
from the Pending Queue using the Management Services Queue (BANQI) screen. 
When a charge is released from the Pending Queue the status of the charge will be updated to ‘R’ 
(Reviewed), so that the charge can be processed by the Charges Posting (CACHPOST) sleeping 
report, which will pass the relevant details to the accounting models for posting. The Charges 
Posting (CACHPOST) report will pass a unique LINE-NUM and hard-coded TRANS-ID = 
‘NAAC’ to be included on the posting record. 
If the charge will settle to a client account without a NBC indicator, then the Charges Posting 
(CACHPOST) report will update the charge status to ‘P’ (Posted) and the relevant details will be 
passed to the accounting models for posting. 
If a charge is deleted from the Pending Queue, the status will be changed from ‘W’ to ‘U’ and the 
amount changed to zero. 
If a charge with a status of ‘W’ is amended so that amount is zero on the Account Charges Review 
and Post (CACRP) screen, the corresponding record will automatically be deleted from the 
Pending Queue. 
If the Charge Settlement Account is blocked, then the posting will be made to the relevant Error 
Suspense Account. The Management Services Queue (BANQI) screen will ensure that any 
Pending Queue items where the Charge Settlement Account is blocked cannot be released.

Maintaining Account Balances 
The system allows you to sweep funds between different accounts in a hierarchy to maintain these 
accounts at their target balance. All these accounts must have the same currency. Before an 
account is eligible to use this functionality, you must complete the relevant details on the Client 
Account Management Services Details (CAEXM) screen.  
The following diagram shows the group hierarchy used for the sweeping of funds between 
accounts: 
Figure C-1. Account Hierarchy 
This process aims to get the grandparent, parent and child accounts to their target balances. Any 
funds left over after this can either be swept to a savings account, invested, or left in the 
grandparent account. The order in which the accounts' target balances are maintained is as follows: 
• 
Child accounts are altered to the target balance, sweeping funds to or from the parent account 
to achieve this. 
• 
Parent accounts are altered to the target balance, sweeping funds to or from the grandparent 
account to achieve this. 
• 
If the Grandparent account is over its target balance, excess funds can be swept to a savings 
account. Alternatively, excess funds can be invested, if the excess is greater than a Minimum 
Investment Amount.  
• 
If the Grandparent account is below its target balance, a loan can be raised to cover the 
difference.  
 
Maintenance of target balances occurs during the overnight run, using the report CASWEOD - 
Sweeps End of Day. This provides a summary showing what operations were carried out, an 
investment report showing what funds are available for investment, and a loan report showing the 
loans required to cover deficits. See the Overnight Reports Guide for more information on this 
report.

Negative Balance Checking 
Accounts can be marked as requiring a Negative Balance Check. Any debit posting made to these 
accounts must be made using a Paired Transaction. When the batch is closed as reconciled, the 
transaction will not be posted to the account, but instead will be sent to the Pending Queue for 
manual authorisation or automatic release by the sleeping report RELPENDQ - Release from 
Pending Queue. See Paired Transactions below for more information.  
Negative Balance Checking can either be performed on all debit transactions entered via the 
Management Services Transaction Maintenance (CATRM) or when preparing the system for the 
Overnight using the report EODPREP – Prepare System for Overnight. 
When using Negative Balance Checking, the following blueprint parameters can be used: 
• 
BP-NBC: This determines whether negative balance checking is applied to clean payments 
• 
BP-NBC-GROUP: Indicates whether Negative Balance Check is to be performed on a single 
client account or available balance of a group of linked client accounts. 
See the Guide to Setting Up for more information on blueprint parameters.

Paired Transactions 
Paired transactions are debit or credit postings to client or general ledger accounts that have been 
paired with a balancing posting to a contra account. The contra account can be either a client or 
general ledger account.  
To enter a paired transaction into the system, you must have an open batch available, and you 
must use the Management Services Transaction Maintenance (CATRM) screen to enter the 
individual transactions. For each type of paired transaction you must enter a Transaction Identifier 
on the Management Services Transaction Details (TRDTM) screen. On this screen you can set up 
the defaults and mandatory fields for each paired transaction type.  
Charges are applicable to paired transactions, but are different from those for other batch posting 
methods. These are called Immediate Charges and are described later in this section. 
You can mark some accounts as requiring a Negative Balance Check before any debit transactions 
can be applied to the account. If you mark an account in this way, it is forced to use paired 
transactions for all its debit transactions. Once the batch containing a debit paired transaction for 
an account has been reconciled, the transaction is moved across to the pending queue, instead of 
being posted to the account. The pending queue can be viewed from the Management Services 
Queue (BANQI) screen.  
Once a paired transaction is on the pending queue, it will remain there until sufficient funds are 
available for it to be processed. The sleeping report RELPENDQ - Release from Pending Queue 
controls which transactions to process, using the following rules:  
• 
Transactions are processed in order of their priority, defined by the Priority Queue Level on 
the Management Services Transaction Details (TRDTM) screen 
• 
If more than one transaction has the same priority, then the smallest debit amount will be 
processed first 
• 
You can override this process and force payment of the transaction  
• 
You can delete the transaction  
 
When processing a transaction, a new batch is created and immediately reconciled. This new batch 
will have a different number from the batch that the transaction was entered in, although the 
original batch number is retained.

Back-valued Paired Transactions 
Back-valued paired transactions can be entered into the system in the same way as normal paired 
transactions. The same rules apply to these back-valued transactions as apply to all back-valued 
postings in the system. These back-valued paired transactions can either be applied directly to the 
account, or placed onto the Back-valued queue for manual release. This is controlled by the 
blueprint parameter BP-POST-BACK-VAL, described in Blueprint Parameters in the Guide to 
Setting Up.  
If you are using a Back-valued queue, you can view these transactions on the Management 
Services Queue (BANQI) screen. The following options are available for release of the 
transaction: 
• 
You can override this process and force payment of the transaction  
• 
You can delete the transaction 
• 
You can process the transaction as if it were an ordinary Paired Transaction. See Paired 
Transactions earlier in this section for more information.  
 
When processing a transaction, a new batch is created and immediately reconciled. This new batch 
will have a different number from the batch that the transaction was entered in, although the 
original batch number is retained. 
Immediate Charges 
Immediate charges are applied to paired transactions entered on the Management Services 
Transaction Maintenance (CATRM) screen. Before an immediate charge can be applied to a 
transaction, it must be set up on the Management Services Immediate Charges (CHRGM) screen.  
The charge is applied immediately to the client account as the transaction is posted into the 
system. If the paired transaction is placed on either the Pending or Back-valued Queue, then the 
charge will also be placed on the Queue. If the transaction is later reversed, then the charge is also 
reversed.

Use this screen to define the paired transactions allowable in the system. On this screen you must 
enter the Transaction Identifier, which is then used on the Management Services Transaction 
Maintenance (CATRM) screen to identify the transaction type.  
You can define which prompts are mandatory for that transaction identifier by adding Narrative 
Prompts. When you create a new transaction using this identifier, these prompts must be 
completed for that transaction.

Management Services Queue (BANQI) 
Use this screen to view the Pending and Back-value authorisation queues that contain paired 
transactions that have been removed from a batch. These queues contain paired transactions that 
require a negative balance check, or are back-valued respectively. This screen can also be used to 
view the Pending Queue for charges that require a negative balance check (see Charges in 
Account Analysis). 
Paired transactions that require a negative balance check are moved to this queue after the batch 
they are entered in is closed. See Paired Transactions earlier in this section for more information. 
They can be released from this queue in the following ways: 
• 
Automatic release via the sleeping report RELPENDQ - Release from Pending Queue. The 
transaction will remain on the queue until sufficient funds are available.  Transactions to the 
same account are processed in order of their priority. When two transactions have the same 
priority, the one with least amount is processed first. 
• 
Manual release can be forced on a transaction, even if the amount will take an account into 
overdraft. 
• 
Deleting a transaction will reverse both the amount of the transaction, and any charges made 
 
Back-valued Paired Transactions are always sent to this queue for authorisation. You can remove 
a back-valued paired transaction in the following ways: 
• 
Ordinary release will apply the paired transaction to the relevant accounts. If the paired 
transaction contains a debit to an account that requires negative balance checking, it will be 
moved to the Pending Queue and processed as above  
• 
Manual release can be forced on a transaction, even if the amount will take an account into 
overdraft. 
• 
Deleting a transaction will reverse both the amount of the transaction, and any charges made 
• 
There is no automatic release from the Back-value Queue 
 
You can change the way that individual paired transactions are removed from the queue they are 
on. To do this, select the method for processing in the 'Action' field adjacent to the transaction you 
want to change, and press the Change button. 
Charges that require a negative balance check are moved to this queue when they are generated by 
the CAACANAL - Account Analysis Statement report. They can be released from this queue in 
the following ways: 
• 
Automatic release via the sleeping report RELPENDQ - Release from Pending Queue. The 
charge will remain on the queue until sufficient funds are available 
• 
Manual release can be forced on a charge, even if the amount will take an account into 
overdraft 
• 
Deleting a charge will change the charge amount to zero and it will not be posted 
 
From the Management Services Queue (BANQI) screen, you can link to the Client Account 
Inquiry (CAACI) screen. To do this, highlight a batch and click the A/C Details button.
